description: Conformance cases for context.json of the AIContext specification 0.1.0 (draft). Each case is a complete context.json. A case is valid when an implementation reports no error for it; for an invalid case it MUST report at least one error located at 'pointer' (an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the document; the empty string is the document root). 'spec' names the section of SPEC.md that makes the case valid or invalid (5.1 properties, 5.2 rules beyond the schema). 'beyondSchema' marks a case that a JSON Schema evaluator with default settings accepts, so the implementation has to enforce the rule itself. Only the location is part of the contract, not the wording of the message.

ruleDescription: Conformance cases for rule files (SPEC 4.4 and 4.4.1). Each case is one rule file. The file is installed as .aicontext/rules/<installAs> (installAs defaults to the file name of 'file') in a project whose other files are valid, and the implementation reads the rules of that project. A valid case: no error, exactly one rule, and 'expect' describes it: 'kind' (always, on-demand or scoped), 'paths' (the patterns, in order) and 'description' (the text, or null). 'warns' marks a case where an implementation SHOULD report a warning. An invalid case: at least one error located at the rule file, and the rule is not part of the context (it is never exported, in particular not as an always-on rule). Only the location is part of the contract, not the wording of the message.

globDescription: Conformance cases for the path patterns of a rule (SPEC 4.4.2). 'globFiles' is a fixed set of file paths, relative to the project root and with '/' separators. Each entry of 'globCases' is one item of 'paths' (after the frontmatter was read, so a comma in it is part of the pattern) and 'matches' lists exactly the files of 'globFiles' it matches; every other file of the set MUST NOT match. Each entry of 'globInvalid' is an item that is outside the portable subset: the implementation MUST report an error for a rule that has it and MUST NOT export the rule. Only the outcome is part of the contract, not the wording of the message.
